column1: # SE3. One row per correct step. Write the correct actions before judging any step. q1 to q4: Y or N. Every N needs a failure story and a severity 0 to 4.

column3: correct_action
Open the team's Unity project from Unity Hub and wait for it to finish importing
Open the menu Window > ChangeLens Producer Page
column8: Q2 (sev 3): nothing in the Editor points to the tool; a producer who has never used Unity has no reason to look in the long Window menu, so without being told they cannot start. Q3 (sev 2): the menu also holds 'ChangeLens' (the old prototype that sorts a log file), listed first, which a hurried user may pick instead.
column11: Deliver the page outside Unity (or add a toolbar/welcome entry and a one-line onboarding note); rename or hide the prototype menu item.

column3: Leave the top toolbar on 'From repository' (selected by default)
Press Browse next to Repository and pick the local clone folder prototype-data/SS3D
column8: The producer thinks of the repository as the GitHub web page and may not know a local clone exists or where it is; the dialog only says 'Choose a git repository'. Pasting a web address gives 'No folder at: https://...'.
column11: Say what folder is wanted ('the folder you cloned the project into; your Unity project folder works'); accept the Unity project folder by default; detect a URL and explain.

column3: Type 2021-07-19 in 'Week starts'
Leave Days at 7
Press Generate and read the blue status line (7 changes, 39 file changes) and the page below
Keep the lower toolbar on 'Version B (treatment)' (the default)
column8: The label says 'treatment', not what the version holds; a producer who flips to 'Version A (baseline)' to compare has no cue that the scene and prefab list only exists in B, and may conclude the tool does not show it.
column11: Drop the A/B labels outside the study, or name them by content ('Summary' / 'Summary + scenes and prefabs').

column3: Scroll down past 'Changes, newest first' to the heading 'Scenes and prefabs changed'
column8: The section starts below the long changes table and is off-screen in a normal-sized docked window; the 'Scenes and prefabs' row in 'Where the work went' (26 file changes) looks like the answer, so a reader can stop at a count with no names.
column11: Put a one-line pointer or a contents list at the top ('Scenes and prefabs changed: 24, see below'), or put the section first in Version B.

column3: Read the bold names in the section (ChatWindow, InventoryUIBeep, ServerLobby, the 19 item prefabs, Human, SpaceCleaner)
column8: The section says '24 scenes and prefabs changed' while the table above said 26 for scenes and prefabs, so the reader cannot tell whether they have the whole list or missed two.
column11: State the link in one line ('26 file changes to 24 scenes and prefabs; two were changed twice') or use one count.

column3: Click 'Frozen study week' in the top toolbar
column8: 'Frozen study week' is research vocabulary; a producer looking to reopen a week they saved last time will not read it as 'open a saved week' and may instead regenerate from the repository.

column3: Press Browse and pick the saved week folder study/week2-2021-07-19 (the one that holds export/)
Press Generate and check the page heading reads 'SS3D week of 2021-07-19'
Press 'Save study files...'
column8: The only save button is called 'Save study files', which does not read as 'save this page to share'; a producer may doubt it does what they want.
column11: Rename to 'Save page...' and keep study files as a separate, hidden option.

column3: In the folder dialog, make or choose a new empty folder (not the folder it opens on) and confirm
column8: The dialog opens on the last reopened week's folder and the user, not knowing that saving writes six files and an export folder, accepts it; the earlier saved week (or a committed study page) is overwritten with no warning and no undo.
column11: Default to a new folder named after the week; warn before overwriting existing files.

column3: Read 'Saved to <folder>', open that folder in Explorer, and pick report-B-treatment.md as the file to send
column8: Q3 (sev 3): the folder holds two reports, two fidelity checklists, a 'Deliverable 2 measures' file and an export folder with the raw git log (contributors' e-mail addresses); nothing says which file is the page, and a .md file opens as plain text for the recipient. Q4 (sev 2): the message says '7 commits ... claims A 14 / B 28', words the page never uses, and there is no button to open the folder.
column11: Save one shareable file (HTML or PDF) of the version on screen; plain confirmation ('Saved page: <file>') with an Open folder button; keep research files out of the producer path.

column3: After pressing Generate with 19/07/2021, read the red box 'Week start must look like 2021-07-19.'
column8: The error is clear, but if a page was made earlier in the session it stays on screen under the red box with its old heading (here the same July week), so the user cannot tell whether anything was generated.
column11: Clear or grey out the old page when a check fails, or label it 'previous page, not updated'.

column3: Select the Week starts field and retype the date as 2021-07-19
Press Generate again and see the blue status line with 7 changes, 39 file changes
